title: architecture-review-kv-cache-splitter-design-notes-2026-03-30
content:
Architecture review meeting notes — KV cache splitter design (follow-up to RFC-142)
Date: 2026-03-30
Attendees: Priya Shah (chair), Carlos Mendes, Liu Wei, Anita Kapoor, Ethan Brooks, Maya Patel (observer)
Context / goal:
- This meeting continues the discussion from RFC-142 (kv-cache sharding) and the March 24th review notes. Primary objective: evaluate the proposed "splitter" component that routes and fragments KV cache entries across shards to reduce hot-spotting and improve multi-model cohabitation.
- Scope: data model for split keys, routing heuristics, consistency guarantees for in-flight requests, and fallback behavior when shards are overloaded. Not covering persistence/replication — handled by a separate follow-up doc.
Agenda:
1) Quick recap of RFC-142 decisions and outstanding questions
2) Splitter design alternatives (centralized vs distributed, static mapping vs dynamic)
3) Consistency & correctness for concurrent requests (KV cache refill, stale prefix handling)
4) Failure and fallback modes (hot shard mitigation, routing to compatible model variants)
5) Action items and ownership
Notes / discussion:
- Recap: RFC-142 established shard boundary as (model-id, quantization-profile, shard-id) and recommended consistent hashing for distribution. Outstanding items: how to split long-lived KV entries / prefixes, and how to route streaming requests that extend prefixes across shards.
- Design alternatives reviewed:
  * Centralized splitter service (single decision plane): simple to reason about routing, easy to instrument, but single point of scheduling contention and potential availability risk.
  * Distributed splitter embedded in frontends (edge decision): lower latency and no central bottleneck; requires robust membership/heartbeat protocol and versioned mapping rollout.
  * Hybrid: a lightweight centralized placement service for long-lived placements + local heuristics for short-lived requests.
- Tradeoffs considered:
  * Consistency vs availability: centralized gives stronger consistency for mapping changes; distributed favors availability and latency. Our SLOs prioritize tail latency for hosted API customers, so distributed approach is attractive but increases complexity for rollouts.
  * Instrumentation and observability: centralized approach simplifies debugging and cost attribution; distributed requires tracing correlation and local metrics aggregation.
- Decision (tentative): proceed with a hybrid approach. Rationale:
  1) Deploy a central placement service that computes initial shard assignments and monitors shard load.
  2) Frontend splitters will cache placement mappings with TTL and subscribe to delta updates. For short-lived or streaming prefixes, frontends use a local heuristic to assign subsequent prefixes to the same shard unless the placement service indicates overload.
  3) In overload cases, the placement service can mark shards as degraded and instruct frontends to apply a fallback routing policy (route to compatible model variant or degrade to a single-shard mode).
- Consistency & in-flight correctness:
  * Problem: a streaming request may generate KV updates that need to be atomically visible on the shard serving subsequent tokens.
  * Proposal: attach placement version to request context. Shard accepts updates only if local placement version matches request version; if mismatch, frontend should either (a) retry with updated mapping, or (b) forward to placement service for synchronous mapping confirmation for that request.
  * This avoids inconsistent reads during mapping changes. Tradeoff: synchronous confirmation adds latency for some requests; we will apply it only when placement TTL has expired or when the frontend detects write failures.
- Hot shard mitigation:
  * Placement service will maintain per-shard load scoring (requests/sec, avg-latency, KV-miss-rate). When score exceeds thresholds, it triggers redistribution via two mechanisms: (1) moving model partitions (for long-lived entries) and (2) instructing frontends to shard prefixes more aggressively (increase split factor).
  * Eviction policy interaction: eviction should be hinted by placement service to prevent premature redistribution churn. We need an eviction-coordination API (follow-up).
- Fallback behavior:
  * If shard is unreachable, frontends try a prioritized list: (1) local retry, (2) route to compatible model variant (same semantics, different shard), (3) degrade to low-cost quantized model with best-effort semantics. This aligns with existing graceful-degradation patterns in the runtime.
Open questions / risks:
- Membership churn: how to ensure frontends have stable views during rolling upgrades? Action: infra team to propose heartbeat/versioning protocol.
- Cost of very frequent placement changes (churn) leading to KV thrash. Need thresholds and cooldowns.
- Edge cases for multi-tenant prefixes where same prefix is hot across different customers — privacy and co-tenancy implications.
- Need to validate latency impact of synchronous placement confirmation on p95/p99.
Action items:
- Carlos: prototype a placement service API (CRUD + delta subscription + per-shard load endpoints). Prototype due: 2026-04-09. Linked ticket: JIRA SRV-1284.
- Liu: implement frontend placement cache with TTL and delta apply logic in the gating branch. Start: 2026-04-01. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4567 (WIP).
- Anita: define eviction-coordination API and a draft spec for eviction hints (doc on Confluence). Due: 2026-04-06.
- Ethan: run perf microbenchmarks for synchronous placement confirmation (impact on p95/p99) and produce a 1-page summary. Due: 2026-04-07.
- Priya: own final design writeup combining prototype findings and produce updated RFC-142 addendum. Due: 2026-04-15.
Follow-ups / next steps:
- Schedule a follow-up architecture sync the week of 2026-04-12 to review prototypes and measurement results.
- Move hybrid design from "tentative" to "final" once placement service prototype demonstrates <5% p95 regression vs baseline.
Notes to reviewers:
- This is an engineering-first working doc; expect iteration. Please comment inline on the Confluence draft linked in linked_artifacts.
- If you have concerns about the fallback semantics or multi-tenant privacy, tag Anita and Priya.
References:
- RFC-142 (kv-cache sharding) — baseline decisions
- Architecture review notes: architecture-review-kv-cache-sharding-meeting-notes-2026-03-03 and follow-ups (see Drive folder)
- JIRA SRV-1284 (placement service epic)
- GitHub PR 4567 (placement cache initial impl)
